item.title: Howden Re highlights reinsurance’s role as a capital tool as prices soften
item.dc:creator: Kane Wells
item.description:
Insurers should treat reinsurance as a capital management tool rather than simply a form of protection, according to Howden Re, which argues that a softening market presents an opportunity to reassess risk retention and improve returns. “The best performers treat reinsurance as a capital tool, not only as protection,” the broker said in a report […]

The post Howden Re highlights reinsurance’s role as a capital tool as prices soften appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Insurers should treat reinsurance as a capital management tool rather than simply a form of protection, according to Howden Re, which argues that a softening market presents an opportunity to reassess risk retention and improve returns.

“The best performers treat reinsurance as a capital tool, not only as protection,” the broker said in a report benchmarking 42 European non-life insurers over 2023-25.

It found that the strongest performers combined good underwriting with leaner capital positions, while some insurers holding the largest solvency buffers generated relatively weak returns.

The capital-light, high-return group held around €28 of capital for every €100 of premium, compared with €86 for the capital-intensive, low-return group. The former averaged a return on equity of around 22%, while the latter returned less than 5%.

Howden Re said the current buyer-friendly reinsurance market, with prices softening, allows insurers to redesign programmes around their capital plans.

This could include reviewing retentions, transferring volatility where they lack an advantage in pricing or data, and protecting against accumulated exposures.

However, the broker stressed that capital efficiency cannot compensate for weak underwriting.

Insurers with the best combined ratios averaged around 17% return on equity, compared with around 4% for those with the weakest, while capital efficiency amplified rather than created good underwriting results.

The report urged insurers to review reinsurance structures against explicit capital and return targets rather than simply renewing existing programmes.

It also called for investment risk to be considered alongside underwriting exposures, as market risk can account for a significant part of an insurer’s capital requirements.

Howden Re cautioned that holding less capital is only beneficial if an insurer can withstand stress, noting that its analysis did not test balance-sheet resilience.

As Reinsurance News understands, the appropriate capital buffer therefore depends on how an insurer would respond to severe but plausible scenarios, rather than how its solvency ratio compares with peers.

The post Howden Re highlights reinsurance’s role as a capital tool as prices soften appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

The post Femia to lead newly launched DOXA Re as President appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
DOXA, a US-based managing general underwriter (MGU) platform, has announced the formation of DOXA Re, a specialty property reinsurance MGU focused on quota share and related proportional solutions for traditional insurers, hybrid carriers and managing general agents (MGAs).

“DOXA Re addresses a growing need for specialty underwriting expertise in the quota share reinsurance marketplace. As MGA and hybrid-carrier programs expand, property placements are becoming more complex, yet access to reinsurers with both the expertise and appetite to participate remains limited,” says DOXA’s chief product and underwriting officer, Joe Guerrero.

Adding: “DOXA Re brings together experienced underwriting, analytics and DOXA’s operational resources to move quickly and thoughtfully to meet the needs of carriers and MGAs.”

James Femia will lead DOXA Re as President, bringing 22 years of property reinsurance underwriting and leadership experience to the position.

Over the course of his career, Femia has built strong partnerships with brokers, cedents, MGAs, and capital markets players while overseeing diverse quota share portfolios.

Under Femia’s leadership, DOXA Re is to establish a balanced portfolio spanning multiple risk classes, product lines, geographic regions, and client segments.

Combining delegated underwriting authority with workflows that support timely reviews and clear communication, DOXA Re aims to provide clients and brokers with continuity from initial review through binding.

Backed by DOXA’s robust operational infrastructure, the MGU will expand its team by recruiting top-tier underwriting and analytics talent committed to rigorous pricing, disciplined risk selection, and thoughtful treaty design.

Femia commented: “Our approach reflects what I call ‘Working Property’: putting capital to work alongside cedents and collaborating with brokers and capacity providers so everyone at the table shares the success.

“We want to be the first call because we know how to navigate risk, capitalize on opportunity and do what we say we will do. That is how we build lasting partnerships and a sustainable business.”

The post Femia to lead newly launched DOXA Re as President appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

The post France riots put SRCC accumulation risk in focus for re/insurers: Morningstar DBRS appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
France’s latest riots are expected to cost insurers no more than €1 billion-€1.2 billion, according to Morningstar DBRS, assuming no further violence. The agency says the unrest reinforces the need to treat strikes, riots and civil commotion (SRCC) as an accumulation risk requiring dedicated pricing, limits and reinsurance.

The latest wave of unrest comes against a backdrop of mass protests over living costs, public spending and government reforms, most notably the Yellow Vest movement of 2018–19, which began over fuel taxes and broader economic grievances.

The current demonstrations began in September 2026, with school students protesting teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and deteriorating facilities. The unrest subsequently broadened to encompass rising fuel prices, the cost of living and dissatisfaction with public services.

Although hundreds of thousands of people joined largely peaceful demonstrations on 17 October, smaller groups engaged in widespread looting, arson and vandalism, including attacks on public buildings in Paris, Marseille and Limoges.

As of 19 October, authorities report around 2,400 arrests and damage to or looting of at least 3,000 businesses. Alexandre Bompard, president of the Retail and Trade Federation, has said the cost to the establishments will run to several hundreds of millions of euros.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has called for localised curfews, while President Emmanuel Macron has ordered a review of security failures.

“Insured losses should remain below EUR 1 to 1.2 billion. Assuming no further violence, we expect the latest French riots to be a manageable earnings event rather than a capital event for the country’s major insurers, particularly after reinsurance recoveries and potential claims against the French State,” Marcos Alvarez, Global head of Insurance, Morningstar DBRS, explained.

The executive also highlighted the implications of France’s planned state-backed riot insurance mechanism, which has been approved but is not yet operational.

Alvarez continued, “The planned framework would introduce mandatory riot coverage and allow insurers to transfer a substantial share of qualifying losses to a State-backed mechanism managed by the Caisse Centrale de Reassurance (CCR), France’s public reinsurer. Because the framework is still pending, the mechanism does not protect insurers against the latest riots.

“Riots are increasingly behaving like natural catastrophes from an insurance perspective. The key risk is having correlated claims across multiple cities at the same time.

“France’s 2023 riots generated about EUR 730 million of insured losses, reinforcing the case for insurers and reinsurers to treat SCCC as an accumulation risk requiring dedicated pricing, limits and reinsurance.”

As Reinsurance News understands, SRCC remains a potential pressure point in reinsurance renewal negotiations, particularly in a softening market where cedants may seek broader coverage on more favourable terms.

However, the latest unrest in France serves as a timely reminder that such events can generate significant, correlated losses across multiple locations.

SRCC should therefore be explicitly priced and carefully managed within reinsurance treaties, rather than treated as a peril that can be added to coverage at little or no additional cost.

The post France riots put SRCC accumulation risk in focus for re/insurers: Morningstar DBRS appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

The post BHSI appoints Carsten Keune as Country Manager for Poland appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance (BHSI), the commercial insurance arm of Berkshire Hathaway, has appointed Carsten Keune as Country Manager for Poland, marking its entry into the Polish market.

BHSI’s entry into Poland aligns with the insurer’s long-term commitment to support regional businesses with local underwriting expertise, responsive claims service, and specialised insurance solutions backed by its financial strength.

In his new role, Keune will be based in Warsaw and lead BHSI’s business in Poland and Central & Eastern Europe, shaping its market strategy and building strong relationships with customers and brokers.

He has extensive insurance experience, deep market knowledge, and proven leadership skills aligning with BHSI’s commitment to investing in experienced talent as it expands across Europe.

Andreas Krause, Head of DACH, BHSI, commented, “Carsten brings the experience, leadership and market insight to advance BHSI’s growth across Central & Eastern Europe.

“He is well suited to establish our presence in Poland, build lasting relationships with customers and brokers, and bring BHSI’s capabilities and long-term approach to businesses across the country.”

BHSI offers a broad range of commercial insurance solutions, including property, casualty, construction, energy, executive and professional lines, marine, and multinational insurance, across Central & Eastern Europe.

The appointment marks another milestone in the insurer’s continued expansion across Central & Eastern Europe.

The post BHSI appoints Carsten Keune as Country Manager for Poland appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: E+S Rück sees growth opportunity in well-structured frequency protection, says CEO
item.dc:creator: Beth Musselwhite
item.description:
Thorsten Steinmann, CEO of E+S Rück and Member of the Executive Board for Hannover Re, said he sees structured solutions as a growth area, with demand increasing for frequency protection and aggregate covers, but stressed that the firm’s appetite for this business depends on adequate margins and well-structured programmes. This afternoon, E+S Rück, the Hannover […]

The post E+S Rück sees growth opportunity in well-structured frequency protection, says CEO appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Thorsten Steinmann, CEO of E+S Rück and Member of the Executive Board for Hannover Re, said he sees structured solutions as a growth area, with demand increasing for frequency protection and aggregate covers, but stressed that the firm’s appetite for this business depends on adequate margins and well-structured programmes.

This afternoon, E+S Rück, the Hannover Re subsidiary responsible for its German property and casualty reinsurance business, held a 2026 Baden-Baden press briefing, exploring current developments in Germany and Continental Europe, alongside the outlook for the upcoming 1 January 2027 renewals.

During the briefing, Steinmann said structured reinsurance is a core segment for E+S Rück, which he considers to have a “market-leading position in structured solutions”.

He explained, “We have a large block of structured solutions. The main purpose is capital solvency or earnings volatility protection. In the last few years, since our clients were doing okay financially, it was mainly an earnings protection type of play, and obviously we have offered one of the few reinsurer solutions which are in the frequency space.

“Since 2023, the attachment points on nat cat programmes went up, and one or another client was super happy with that and went through the last three years very easily with these high attachment points, and is now happy to keep that stable. While some others started to buy lower down or frequency protections, sometimes in the form of an aggregate, sometimes in the form of a non-traditional frequency protection.”

Steinmann noted that this is a growing line of business and expects some clients who have not yet bought frequency protection to start looking into it. He stressed that, if structured properly and priced adequately, there is an opportunity for E+S Rück.

“We do expect that some clients will seek some sort of frequency protection or aggregate covers, and I can say we have always been a market participant who has had appetite for well-structured frequency protections and aggregate covers, and we continue to do so as long as the margins are okay and the programmes are well structured,” he said.

Steinmann also outlined E+S Rück’s outlook for the January renewals across Europe.

“We see, on the one hand, a picture of increasing complexity, but at the same time also continued opportunity,” he explained. “The good thing is the underlying demand for reinsurance remains strong, while we expect the market to remain competitive and capacity to be readily available.

“Natural catastrophe remains a growth area for us. This has some historic reasons. We are a little bit underrepresented in the nat cat space and we have corrected this over the last three to four years, but we are not there yet.

“Climate change, inflation, and increasing concentration of values continue to drive demand for protection. And at the same time, we do expect that some clients will seek some sort of frequency protection or aggregate covers.”

The post E+S Rück sees growth opportunity in well-structured frequency protection, says CEO appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

The post Ray Lei named Product Proposition Lead for Greater China, Markel International appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Markel International has expanded its Asian leadership team with the appointment of Ray Lei as Greater China Product Proposition Lead.

In her new role, Lei will work closely with teams across the region to strengthen product proposition, support the firm’s brokers and clients, and help drive the next phase of growth in Greater China.

She has nearly 15 years of extensive industry experience, having started her career at HDI-Gerling Industrie Versicherung AG as a Technical Assistant in 2012.

After this, Lei spent nearly 14 years with AXA General Insurance Hong Kong Limited, serving in roles of increasing importance. At the firm, she most recently served as the Head of Reinsurance Hub Management for General Insurance.

Prior to this, she was the Senior Manager for Technical and Innovation, Reinsurance Team Lead, and Assistant Actuarial Manager.

Lei started her career at AXA General Insurance Hong Kong as an Actuarial Assistant, later serving as Actuarial Analyst and Senior Actuarial Analyst.

The insurer, in a statement, added, “As our business continues to evolve, we’re delighted to welcome Ray’s expertise, market insight, and fresh perspective to Markel.”

In related news, Markel recently raised its London Fine Art & Specie capacity from USD 100 million to USD 250 million through Lloyd’s of London to accommodate rising demand.

The post Ray Lei named Product Proposition Lead for Greater China, Markel International appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: Fitch raises Allstate’s ratings following improvements in capital and underwriting performance
item.dc:creator: Taylor Mixides
item.description:
Fitch Ratings, a global credit rating agency, has upgraded the credit ratings of The Allstate Corporation, a US insurance provider specialising in property, casualty and personal insurance products. The decision reflects stronger capitalisation, continued underwriting profitability and improvements in the company’s financial position. Fitch has assigned a Stable Outlook to all the ratings. In an […]

The post Fitch raises Allstate’s ratings following improvements in capital and underwriting performance appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Fitch Ratings, a global credit rating agency, has upgraded the credit ratings of The Allstate Corporation, a US insurance provider specialising in property, casualty and personal insurance products.

The decision reflects stronger capitalisation, continued underwriting profitability and improvements in the company’s financial position. Fitch has assigned a Stable Outlook to all the ratings.

In an announcement issued on 15 October 2026, Fitch Ratings confirmed that the Insurer Financial Strength (IFS) ratings of Allstate’s principal property and casualty (P&C) insurance subsidiaries had risen to ‘A+’ from ‘A’.

The agency also raised Allstate’s holding company Issuer Default Rating (IDR) to ‘A-’ from ‘BBB+’, while the ratings for senior unsecured debt increased to ‘BBB+’ from ‘BBB’. All ratings retain a Stable Outlook.

Fitch attributed the upgrades primarily to a stronger assessment of Allstate’s capital position and its consistent underwriting results. The agency also cited the insurer’s established market presence and competitive position in the US personal-lines sector as supporting factors. However, Fitch noted that the company’s exposure to riskier investments remains higher than the industry average, limiting its overall credit assessment.

Fitch identified Allstate’s market position as a key strength, with the insurer ranking as the fourth-largest provider of private-passenger motor insurance and the second-largest homeowners’ insurer in the US, measured by direct written premiums in 2025. Fitch said the company benefits from its scale, extensive distribution network and advanced pricing capabilities, which help maintain its competitive position.

Allstate’s operations are primarily focused on personal insurance, supplemented by protection services and a smaller commercial insurance business. According to Fitch Ratings, the company reaches customers through a combination of exclusive agents, independent agents and direct sales channels.

The agency also pointed to improvements in Allstate’s underwriting results. The company’s GAAP combined ratio fell to 85.2% in 2025 from 94.3% in the previous year. Fitch attributed this change to stronger underwriting margins and a greater contribution from favourable reserve development. The underlying combined ratio, which provides a view of underwriting performance excluding certain effects, also improved, declining to 79.4% from 84.6%.

Fitch said the improvement continued during the first six months of 2026, when Allstate recorded a GAAP combined ratio of 84.3% and an underlying combined ratio of 79.8%. The agency expects underwriting profitability to remain robust as the company expands its distribution channels and develops more affordable insurance offerings to support growth. Nevertheless, Fitch cautioned that claims costs and catastrophe-related losses could affect future results.

Allstate’s capital position has strengthened alongside its underwriting performance. Fitch Ratings reported that higher earnings had helped rebuild the company’s financial buffer against insurance and investment risks. Statutory surplus reached USD $21.6 billion at the end of 2025, up from USD $17.1 billion at the end of 2024. Over the same period, statutory operating leverage decreased from 3.1 times to 2.6 times.

Although statutory operating leverage remains above historical levels, Fitch expects further progress as Allstate continues to generate capital and premium growth becomes more moderate. The agency also confirmed that the company retained a ‘Strong’ result under Fitch’s Prism capital model at the end of 2025, supported by the contribution of earnings to capital generation.

The company’s financial leverage also moved lower, falling to 18.1% in the first half of 2026 from 19.8% at the end of 2025. Fitch Ratings attributed the reduction to growth in shareholders’ equity and expects leverage to remain broadly around its current level over the near term.

Investment risk continues to represent a relative weakness in Allstate’s credit profile. Fitch Ratings assessed the company’s investment and asset risk several notches below its IFS rating, reflecting its comparatively high exposure to riskier assets. The agency expects this exposure to remain elevated, given the insurer’s investments in equities and performance-based assets.

However, the company’s risky asset ratio showed an improvement, falling to 76.0% at the end of 2025 from 86.2% a year earlier. Fitch explained that the decline reflected shareholders’ equity increasing at a faster rate than the company’s risky asset holdings. While the agency viewed this development favourably, it indicated that the ratio would need to remain at or below its current level over a sustained period before a stronger assessment could be considered.

Fitch also reported improvements in Allstate’s capacity to meet its debt obligations, alongside continued access to substantial liquidity resources. The insurer’s GAAP fixed-charge coverage ratio increased to 26.6 times in 2025, considerably above its average of 9.8 times over the preceding five years. Fitch linked the improvement to the company’s stronger financial performance.

Liquidity and financial flexibility remained strong during the first half of 2026. Fitch reported that Allstate held USD $9.45 billion in assets at the holding-company level that could be converted into cash within three months. The agency estimated that these resources represented approximately 18 times the company’s annual interest expense and preferred dividends.

Overall, Fitch Ratings’ upgrades reflect the combination of stronger capitalisation, sustained underwriting profitability and reduced financial leverage, supported by Allstate’s established position in the US insurance market. The Stable Outlook applies to all upgraded ratings, while the insurer’s exposure to riskier investments remains an important consideration in Fitch’s assessment of its creditworthiness.

The post Fitch raises Allstate’s ratings following improvements in capital and underwriting performance appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: Howden Re strengthens US casualty team with two senior appointments
item.dc:creator: Taylor Mixides
item.description:
Howden Re, the reinsurance broking and advisory business of Howden Group, has announced two senior appointments to its US casualty team, strengthening its broking, actuarial and analytical capabilities. The company said the appointments build on its investment in its US casualty practice since 2023, with the aim of enhancing the expertise and support available to […]

The post Howden Re strengthens US casualty team with two senior appointments appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Howden Re, the reinsurance broking and advisory business of Howden Group, has announced two senior appointments to its US casualty team, strengthening its broking, actuarial and analytical capabilities.

The company said the appointments build on its investment in its US casualty practice since 2023, with the aim of enhancing the expertise and support available to clients.

Matthew Kuczwaj joins Howden Re as Managing Director, Casualty Actuarial, with more than 25 years of actuarial experience across reinsurance and broking. Jackson Fairweather has been appointed Director, Casualty Broking. He has nearly a decade of experience in casualty treaty reinsurance, alongside established relationships with clients and market participants across the US.

Carrie Byler, Managing Director, Head of US General Casualty, Howden Re, said: “As our Casualty business grows, we are investing in the experience our clients receive. Jackson brings deep casualty treaty expertise and strong relationships across the US market. He will help us deliver an exceptional service to clients at every stage of the placement, from structuring through to execution.”

Evan Glisson, Managing Director, Global Head of Casualty Analytics, Howden Re, added: “Our clients need clear, data-driven insight to make confident decisions about their portfolios. Matt’s actuarial expertise adds real depth to our analytics capability and will help us give clients the insights they need to achieve their strategic goals.”

The post Howden Re strengthens US casualty team with two senior appointments appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: Bajaj Finserv announces establishment of new reinsurance subsidiary
item.dc:creator: Kassandra Jimenez-Sanchez
item.description:
Bajaj Finserv, a leading Indian financial services holding company, has incorporated a new wholly owned subsidiary, Bajaj Reinsurance Limited, marking its formal entry into the reinsurance sector. The company disclosed the development in regulatory filings to the BSE and the National Stock Exchange of India on October 17, 2026, confirming receipt of the Certificate of […]

The post Bajaj Finserv announces establishment of new reinsurance subsidiary appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Bajaj Finserv, a leading Indian financial services holding company, has incorporated a new wholly owned subsidiary, Bajaj Reinsurance Limited, marking its formal entry into the reinsurance sector.

The company disclosed the development in regulatory filings to the BSE and the National Stock Exchange of India on October 17, 2026, confirming receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

According to the announcement, the venture remains subject to subject to necessary regulatory approvals.

The move formalises plans previously approved by the Bajaj Finserv Board to pursue reinsurance operations. Some industry reports have suggested that former GIC Re chairman N Ramaswamy Narayanan will lead the venture.

Headquartered in Pune, Maharashtra, Bajaj Finserv serves as the financial arm of the Bajaj Group, operating across lending, insurance, wealth management and digital payments through its various subsidiaries.

It currently has operations in life and general insurance through Bajaj Life Insurance and Bajaj General Insurance.

The new reinsurance business would add another part of the insurance value chain to the group’s existing operations. The move would also come as India seeks to build out its domestic reinsurance capacity.

The post Bajaj Finserv announces establishment of new reinsurance subsidiary appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.

item.title: Brit extends cyber insurance distribution through Acturis Package
item.dc:creator: Taylor Mixides
item.description:

The development is intended to make Brit’s cyber insurance products more accessible to brokers and support greater efficiency when arranging cover for clients. […]

The post Brit extends cyber insurance distribution through Acturis Package appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
item.content:encoded:
Brit Group Holdings Limited (Brit), an insurer offering specialist insurance products for businesses, has further expanded its digital distribution through the Acturis platform with the introduction of Brit Cyber on Acturis Package.

The development is intended to make Brit’s cyber insurance products more accessible to brokers and support greater efficiency when arranging cover for clients.

The latest launch follows the introduction of Brit Cyber on Acturis CyberNow in May. According to Brit, making its cyber offering available through Acturis Package will allow brokers to consider cyber insurance alongside package policies, helping them recognise potential coverage requirements earlier in the sales process. Brit said the integration would also support brokers in providing clients with protection against emerging cyber risks.

Domenic Provenzano, UK E-Trading Business Development Manager at Brit, commented: “We are pleased to be launching on Acturis Package, which comes as the next phase of our digital trading journey. By expanding our presence across the Acturis platform, we can continue to deliver our market-leading underwriting proposition to a wider customer base, ensuring that brokers and their clients can access our solutions as efficiently as possible.”

Adelle Gruber, Class Underwriter, Cyber at Brit, added: “Our expanded presence on Acturis reflects our commitment to providing brokers with greater choice and access to our products through efficient distribution, with Brit continuing to be well-placed to meet clients’ evolving needs. This is particularly important as demand continues to grow among firms of all sizes for protection against cyber risks, amid an increasingly volatile market landscape. It will also ensure that brokers can quickly access our expertise and efficiently place cover for clients, supporting profitable growth through enhanced digital trading capabilities.”

The post Brit extends cyber insurance distribution through Acturis Package appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws.
